### Also covered by

Riehl, *Category Theory in Context* (2nd ed.), §2.1 Example 2.1.6, clause (i), printed p. 57 (PDF pp. 77–78) — item `riehl:2.1:example6`. Riehl states the contravariant power-set functor to be represented by the two-element set of truth values via characteristic functions, and spells out the naturality clause this issue supplies: *precomposing a classifying map with f computes the preimage along f*, which is exactly the lemma `char (sub_reindex f s) ≈ char s ∘ f`.

- [ ] (from Riehl §2.1) `Structure/Topos.v:71–73` glosses `classifier_classifies` as making "subobjecthood representable"; the appositive that follows it (every mono is the pullback of a generic mono along a unique classifying map) is what is actually proved, but the word "representable" describes the natural isomorphism `Sub ≅ [Hom ─,Ω]` that the tree does not yet state. Update that header once the natural isomorphism exists, or correct it if it does not.

### Also covered by

Riehl, *Category Theory in Context* (2nd ed.), §2.2 Theorem 2.2.4, printed p. 61 (PDF pp. 81–83) — item `riehl:2.2:thm4`. Riehl also records a size observation — that the collection of natural transformations out of a representable is a genuinely small set even when C is only locally small — which in this library is discharged silently by universe polymorphism rather than being a theorem.

- [ ] (from Riehl §2.2) `Functor/Hom/Yoneda.v:22`'s header comment claims the Yoneda isomorphism is "natural in both A and F"; that claim is currently unsupported anywhere in the tree. Riehl, *Category Theory in Context* (2nd ed.), §2.2 Remark 2.2.7, printed p. 63 (PDF p. 83) — item `riehl:2.2:remark7`. Riehl reads the Yoneda lemma, for small C, as the assertion that the represented functor C(c,−), viewed as an object of the functor category, **represents** the evaluation functor `ev_c : Set^C ⟶ Set`, F ↦ F c — the formulation that captures naturality in F but not in c, and so motivates the two-variable version this issue builds. The evaluation *bifunctor* is in this issue's scope; the partially applied functor and the representability packaging are not.

### Also covered by

Riehl, *Category Theory in Context* (2nd ed.), §2.2 Corollary 2.2.11, printed p. 65 (PDF pp. 85–86) — item `riehl:2.2:cor11`. Riehl derives Cayley's theorem from the covariant Yoneda embedding applied to a group regarded as a one-object category: the embedding carries the unique object to the right regular G-set, its G-equivariant endomorphisms are the left multiplications, and composing with the faithful forgetful functor to sets exhibits G as a subgroup of the symmetric group on its underlying set.

A same-name trap worth recording in the file header: `Construction/Cayley.v` does **not** prove Cayley's theorem for groups. It states no group, no action and no permutation group; it carries no `Faithful To_Cayley` instance; and its only lemmas beyond the category (`Cayley_Right`/`Cayley_Left`, `:179`/`:191`) are Leibniz-`=` reassociation facts gated on an extra strict-unit hypothesis.

- [ ] (from Riehl §2.2) The step Riehl's proof turns on is proved: every G-equivariant endomorphism of the right regular G-set is automatically an automorphism, so the embedding lands in the automorphism group

append_block:
### Also covered by

Riehl, *Category Theory in Context* (2nd ed.), §2.1 Example 2.1.6, clause (iv), printed p. 57 (PDF pp. 77–78) — item `riehl:2.1:example6`. Riehl states the currying bijection in **representable** form: the contravariant functor `X ↦ Set(X × A, B)` is *represented by* the exponential set `B^A`, and she names the representing natural isomorphism as currying itself.

This is the same mathematical content as this issue's currying adjunction, so the adjunction packaging remains the shared deliverable. One increment is genuinely new and is NOT discharged by the Definition of Done above:

- [ ] (from Riehl §2.1 Example 2.1.6(iv)) Exhibit the bijection as a **`Representable` instance**, not only as an `Adjunction`. `Functor/Representable.v:46` defines `Class Representable`, but the class is inert tree-wide — zero instances and zero consumers — so no in-tree functor is currently witnessed as representable at all. Instantiating it for `X ↦ Set(X × A, B)` with representing object `B^A` (or, in a general CCC, for the corresponding hom-functor) is the first such witness and is what makes Riehl's phrasing true in-tree rather than merely derivable.

Scope note for the same item: clauses **(vi)** (singular cohomology with coefficients in `A` represented by the Eilenberg–MacLane space `K(A,n)` on homotopy classes of CW complexes) and **(vii)** (principal `G`-bundles represented by a classifying space `BG`) are **OUT OF SCOPE** for this library — it has no homotopy theory, no CW complexes and no bundle theory, and nothing in tree is a near-miss for either. They are recorded here so that Example 2.1.6 is fully accounted for across its seven clauses rather than silently truncated: (i) → #721, (ii)–(iii) and (v) → the Top and Vect_k representability issues filed from this chapter, (iv) → here, (vi)–(vii) → out of scope.
